PullRequest.Title: chat: Move MCP and plugin discovery to Customizations

## Description

Stacked on #340337.

Moves MCP and plugin discovery out of the default Extensions marketplace display now that the Customizations marketplace provides the same functionality.

- Removes the default installed/marketplace panes for MCP servers and agent plugins from Extensions.
- Shows a focused handoff screen for `@mcp` searches with a **Browse MCP Servers** action that opens MCP results in Customizations Discover.
- Opens installed MCP servers in the Customizations MCP section and routes the Agent Plugins browse command to the Customizations plugin marketplace.
- Adds **Show Plugins** to the configured-marketplace quick pick and opens plugin results in Customizations.

## Testing

- `npm run compile` — passed
- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\actions\chatPluginActions.test.ts` — passed, 4 tests
- `npm run eslint -- src\vs\workbench\contrib\mcp\browser\mcpServersView.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\mcp\browser\mcpCommands.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\browser\agentPluginsView.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\browser\actions\chatPluginActions.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\actions\chatPluginActions.test.ts` — passed
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed line, selected-ref control flow, undefined-source discovery request, all-source expansion, Promise.all fan-out, and per-source marketplace fetch are all directly traced. Only the exact number of configured sources and cold-cache latency vary by user.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Parallel network requests and filesystem reads for configured plugin marketplace repositories
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each click fans out to every enabled configured plugin marketplace, so cold work and aggregate concurrency grow linearly with the number of configured marketplaces rather than remaining one request/read for the marketplace the user selected.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased marketplace-open latency and an avoidable burst of network/filesystem work; one slow unrelated marketplace can hold up the combined first page.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this diff the per-marketplace management quick pick had no “Show Plugins” operation and initiated no catalog fetch. The new operation is entered after selecting one concrete `ref`, so the necessary new work can be bounded to that one source.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new branch invokes `OpenMarketplace` with only the generic Plugins section and drops `ref.canonicalId`. Discovery therefore leaves `selectedSourceId` undefined and queries all enabled sources.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `executeCommand` call at line 311 introduces the browse operation but omits the marketplace identifier that is available as `ref.canonicalId`, causing all-source discovery instead of a singleton-source query.
Findings.Title: Scope “Show Plugins” to the selected marketplace
Findings.Impact: With several configured GitHub or cloned-repository marketplaces, choosing “Show Plugins” for one marketplace loads every marketplace concurrently and the discovery service awaits all providers before returning the page. Cold GitHub sources perform network reads and cloned sources perform repository filesystem reads, including unrelated or slow sources.
Findings.Evidence: The containing flow has already selected a concrete `ref`, but line 311 passes only `AICustomizationManagementSection.Plugins`. `AICustomizationDiscoveryPage.loadCatalog` consequently sends `sourceIds: undefined`; `queryEnabledCustomizationMarketplaceSources` expands that to every enabled source; `CustomizationMarketplaceService.query` invokes every selected provider with `Promise.all`. Each `PluginCustomizationMarketplaceProvider` then calls `queryMarketplacePlugins` for its own canonical marketplace, and the underlying fetch performs GitHub network or cloned-repository filesystem work. The discovery tests also establish that selecting a source changes requests from `sourceIds: undefined` to a singleton source ID.
Findings.Recommendation: Pass the selected marketplace source through the command target (using its existing customization marketplace source ID) and initialize Discover with that source selected, so the first query has a singleton `sourceIds` value; retain the source picker so users can broaden the search explicitly.

Scenarios.Scenario: Choose a configured plugin marketplace in Manage Plugin Marketplaces, then select Show Plugins
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The quick pick first awaits one repository existence check, then opens the Customizations editor. Available results require the discovery catalog query to complete; its combined first page awaits every enabled provider.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check whether the selected marketplace repository directory exists
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one call for the selected marketplace
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same existence check already ran for marketplace management.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the action quick pick is shown

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch plugin definitions from configured GitHub marketplaces
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one cold fetch per enabled configured GitHub marketplace, N in total
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This per-marketplace management flow had no Show Plugins operation and issued no catalog fetch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All provider promises must settle before the combined first page is available

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read plugin definitions from cloned/local marketplace repositories
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one repository traversal/read per enabled configured non-GitHub marketplace, included in N
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This management flow did not query marketplace contents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All provider promises must settle before the first page is available

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number N of enabled configured plugin marketplaces after canonical-ID deduplication; each configured plugin source is a separate provider.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The catalog service invokes all N selected providers concurrently with Promise.all and has no shared limiter. Each provider scopes its own read to one marketplace, but the command fails to select just the marketplace already chosen by the user.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold GitHub marketplaces perform remote reads and cloned repositories perform filesystem reads. GitHub marketplace data has a persisted cache, so warm runs may avoid network, while discovery continuations only cache pagination and the editor-local browse cache does not apply to the non-empty @type:plugin query. Reusing the open editor can retain loaded state, but the cold command still fans out.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the selected ref is dropped at the changed command call, discovery sends no sourceIds, enabled-source expansion selects all sources, and the marketplace service invokes them with Promise.all.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Most users likely configure few marketplaces and warm GitHub caches reduce transport cost, but enterprise policy and workspace settings can add multiple sources and any slow source delays the aggregate request.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable boundary fan-out: a per-marketplace action unnecessarily queries every configured plugin source instead of the selected singleton source.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command opens the Customizations editor and sets Discover to @type:plugin. Rendering available results waits for the customization marketplace query.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider query per enabled plugin-capable source
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old Extensions search called PluginMarketplaceService.fetchMarketplacePlugins, which also fanned out across all configured marketplace references concurrently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Results wait for the combined catalog page

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read path per configured non-GitHub marketplace on a cold query
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old @agentPlugins view used the same plugin marketplace service and repository reads.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Enabled plugin marketplace sources after deduplication, plus enabled platform sources that support plugin media types.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Customization providers are queried concurrently with Promise.all. Providers that do not support plugin media types return without a transport call.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configured GitHub repositories can use persisted cache; cloned repositories use filesystem state. The open editor is singleton-style, so repeated commands reuse the pane and its loaded discovery state where possible.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the route and query behavior; insufficient evidence that its effective expensive-boundary count is worse than the old all-marketplaces search.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The Customizations editor allocates broader UI than the former list view, but no concrete additional scaling boundary beyond the intended catalog query was established for this route.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the route changes UI ownership, but the old command already queried all configured plugin marketplaces and no high-confidence boundary-count regression was proven.

Scenarios.Scenario: Search @mcp in Extensions and use Browse MCP Servers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The Extensions search now renders only a local handoff page, with no gallery query. The catalog boundary starts only after the user presses Browse MCP Servers; Customizations results then wait for enabled MCP-capable providers.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero on the initial @mcp search; after the explicit button click, one query per enabled MCP-capable source
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old @mcp marketplace view immediately called IMcpWorkbenchService.queryGallery, generally one gallery query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the initial search path; required for marketplace results after the handoff action

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number M of enabled MCP-capable marketplace sources; plugin-only providers are invoked but return immediately from media-type filtering.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The customization marketplace queries M expensive providers concurrently via Promise.all; no extra request starts on the initial @mcp search.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The discovery page retains loaded catalog state while the singleton editor remains open. Provider-specific cache behavior applies; the removed Extensions gallery path previously used its own gallery service paging.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for deferred boundary placement and provider concurrency.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact enabled MCP source set depends on product and user configuration, but the initial search path clearly removes rather than adds remote work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the changed initial search defers network work until explicit browsing, and broader provider coverage after that action is intentional marketplace behavior.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command now opens the singleton Customizations editor and selects the MCP section. Editor construction and local list rendering are on the UI critical path; optional connector refresh is started asynchronously and is not awaited by the command.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One local installed-state query in the former narrow view; the new editor primarily consumes existing service state
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old installed view called queryLocal once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The former view awaited this before showing its model

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh Copilot connectors when that feature is enabled
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one request when the MCP section becomes visible
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old installed-MCP view did not request connectors.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Started asynchronously and not awaited by editor opening

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Installed MCP servers, plugins, and customization sections represented by the broader editor; optional connector count is remote-service-defined.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Local widget refreshes are event-driven. If connectors are enabled, one connector request is started; no per-installed-server network fan-out was found.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The editor input is singleton-style and warm opens reuse the pane. MCP services retain local state; cold editor construction creates all built-in section widgets, while gallery snapshots remain gated by visibility/configuration.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the command route and widget lifecycle; lower for material user-visible magnitude.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold editor DOM/allocation cost is broader than the old view, but the optional remote request is off the critical path and no measured or collection-amplified regression sufficient for a finding was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: broader eager UI work exists, but the only new expensive boundary is configuration-gated, singular, cancellable, and off the critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup and default Extensions view registration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Contribution constructors register remaining search-only views and actions during workbench startup. Removed default MCP/plugin panes and the installed-plugin context autorun no longer initialize or react in the default Extensions display.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of installed plugins/servers and subsequent plugin observable updates.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No changed subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundary was found on this registration path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Not cache-dependent; removed registrations reduce retained descriptors/listeners and avoid constructing those panes unless reached through remaining search surfaces.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that work was removed; no blame-worthy regression-fix evidence was established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The savings are not quantified and do not establish that this PR fixes a shipped regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: this path is neutral-to-improving for startup and retained UI work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and traced the new Customizations command paths, editor lifecycle, provider fan-out, cache behavior, and filesystem/network boundaries. Reported one medium-confidence-severity boundary fan-out where a per-marketplace action drops its selected source and queries every configured plugin marketplace. Other routes either defer work, reuse equivalent pre-existing fan-out, or add only bounded/off-critical-path work.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
